newsitem.title: USA: Gateway's president, COO to step down.
newsitem.headline: Gateway's president, COO to step down.

text.p: Gateway 2000 Inc on Monday said its president and chief operating officer, Richard Snyder, was leaving his posts to lead an entrepreneurial venture capital fund.
A search for a successor has been launched, the company said. Synder will continue to serve on Gateway's board.
Synder is leaving to lead a venture capital fund to be headquartered near Ann Arbor, Michigan, Gateway said.

Before joining Gateway six year ago, Snyder was a partner with the accounting firm Coopers & Lybrand in Chicago. Before that, he was a tax partner with the firm in Detroit. He also served as an adjunct professor of accounting at the University of Michigan from 1982 to 1984.

"Rick has been an outstanding asset of Gateway 2000 for these last six years. His leadership has taken us from a small direct manufacturer of desktop computers to a Fortune 500 worldwide leader of home and corporate computing. We are sad to see Rick leave but we wish him well in his new endeavor," Ted Waitt, Gateway's chairman and chief executive, said in a statement.

Snyder commented, "I leave a great many memories behind, but I am looking forward to this opportunity and the chance to return to my family's home in Michigan. I have enjoyed being part of the team that launched a great American corporation, but I am happy that I will get the chance to work with a whole new group of technology entrepreneurs as they attempt to build the next Gateway."
